answer: Propose a quartz ticket: each established sponsor may sign just one newcomer, ever. A willow tree of sponsor ancestry requires three root-disjoint tickets for reward eligibility; an echo from a sibling branch is void. The ledger burns each sponsor quota on use. A farm can share a model or buy signatures, but each clone consumes three distinct lifetime slots: even three farm-owned sponsors yield only one new sponsor, so borrowing money cannot replenish the finite roster. If a sponsor signs twice, a ledger audit forfeits its bond. Skip a ticket and the clone earns nothing.
